Senses.Explanation: A ceremonial scepter used from the teaching seat: the records raise it, draw a circle with it, or personify it as an interlocutor before the assembly. This is a handled implement, distinct from the wish-fulfilling jewel compound and from the monastery name Huangshan Ruyi Cloister.
Senses.Note: The full-case reading separates the action-stage directions from Guxue Zhe's personification of the implement.

Senses.Explanation: In the compound for a wish-fulfilling jewel (如意寶), the word belongs to that jewel image. Yongming Yanshou and Baizhang Huaihai use the jewel-name in expositions; neither passage refers to the handheld teaching scepter.
Senses.Note: This is a different referent, not a different reading of the implement.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (宗鏡錄): The exact headword speaker is Yongming Yanshou. Yongming's authorial exposition says a good friend seeks the one mind (為如意寶), a wish-fulfilling jewel.

Senses.Explanation: In the name Huangshan Ruyi Cloister (黃山如意院), Ruyi is the proper name of a monastery. The biography uses it as a place-name and supplies no evidence that the cloister is the ceremonial implement or the wish-fulfilling jewel.
Senses.Note: Proper-name sense; one work, therefore provisional.
